purpose: Check whether a frozen language-conditioned estimate of an object's metric extent is independent evidence for its physical identity in a relational expression.
primary_panel: Previously unused ordinary physical returns. Two distinct annotated visible same-class subjects project on the same half of the image. Use both opposite-side and same-side/changing-landmark counterfactuals when available. Freeze the roster before model predictions. Raw annotations exclusively for test construction and post-seal evaluation.
ordinary_controls: All prior 576 ordinary panel rows and 168 natural rows, including fallbacks. Reuse the previous 100 changing-landmark and 268 opposite-side rows as exposed comparisons.
evidence: For each native backbone seed, decode every isolated class noun with identical anchor and companion seed batch. Compare the resulting metric box extent to a physical component measured from the returns. A role reads frozen word evidence times paired metric compatibility. Compare same-scene unpaired category extent, wrongly assigned noun, wrong reference and image-only rules.
hypothesis: The noun-specific local metric prediction brings correct physical subjects and reference instances ahead of alternative objects when the image center cannot settle the two utterances.
evaluation: Count paired both-subject and four-endpoint correctness by independent oriented IoU and seed ownership. Use same-physical-frame and recording units. Directional Acc25/50, changes and all failures. Apply previously sealed bottom-face rule to the identical predicted instance for an additional post-selection geometry comparison. No threshold choice using target labels.
decision: Evaluate local shape against both the same-evidence controls and frozen lexical-only reading, with identity precision on natural descriptions and ordinary grounding. Zero/negative or indistinguishable benefit does not support this method. Geometry and semantic decisions judged separately.
